title: Phase Structured Electron Beams to Probe Chiral Plasmons
content: Surface plasmons (SPs), excitations of electron oscillations along a dielectric interface, are the subject of much research for potential technology applications [1]. Modern scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) has utilized aberration-corrected probes with low energy spread to precisely map the surface plasmon structure of nanoparticles using electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) [2]. Despite the great precision of these measurements, there is often phase and symmetry information in the plasmonic structure that traditional STEM EELS is unable to resolve. Some modes may be dark or inseparable from other modes due to overlap in space and frequency even while having different symmetry. Structuring the electron wavefunction allows the beam to be tailored to the symmetries or chirality of the sample’s surface plasmon structure [3]. We will discuss calculations of structured beams interacting with SPs, experimental progress, and the technical considerations necessary for the practical realization in a TEM.
